questions.q: What is the author's central point about confidence?
options: Maximum confidence is the key to success
Confidence is inborn and cannot change
The right amount of confidence matters, not the most
questions.explain: He argues confidence isn't about having more but calibrating the right amount.

questions.q: What did Burrow's coach notice about him when he was nine?
options: His blood pressure seemed the same whether shooting, mowing, or rescuing someone
His blood pressure spiked whenever he shot free throws in tight games
His heart rate stayed lower in games than at practice or at home
His stamina outlasted every other player on the AAU team in each game
questions.explain: The coach said his blood pressure appeared the same across tasks, so he was unfazed regardless of the task.

questions.q: How long was Burrow a backup at Ohio State?
questions.explain: He spent three years as a backup, largely watching from the sideline.

questions.q: What phrase did McRaven use for what he wanted in a SEAL?
options: Just enough swagger and just enough humility
questions.explain: McRaven wanted someone with 'just enough swagger, but also just enough humility.'

questions.q: What does the author think the coach's comment was really aimed at?
questions.explain: He believes the coach was directing his comments at Burrow's parents, about channeling the confidence.
